description:
Found by the fz-kdt.120 build (2026-09-03, c2c723c63), which had to rewrite a
fixture header and then explain 36 canon diff lines that meant nothing.

The `--dump backend=` canonical form is this arc`s faithful comparand and the
one gates rely on. But it renders SPANS AS BYTE OFFSETS into the fixture
source, so editing a fixture`s COMMENT text -- without touching a single line
of code, and without changing the line COUNT -- shifts every subsequent offset
and the fixture reads as a canon mover. The artifact is identical.

REPRODUCER: change one word inside the header comment of
`fixtures2/behavior/spec_shared_var_self_composition.fz` without changing its
line count, then `fz2 interp --dump backend=<file>` before and after and diff:
36 span lines move, artifact unchanged. (Flag order matters -- writing
`--log-telemetry` after the subcommand truncates the fixture, fz-kdt.215.)

WHY IT MATTERS: every ticket in this arc measured "canon movers vs base" to
decide whether a change was behaviour-neutral, and a ticket that also edits a
fixture`s prose gets a false positive it must then explain away by hand. It
also means two trees whose fixtures differ only in comments cannot be compared
on canon at all.

THE FIX: render a span in a form that is stable under source edits that do not
change the code -- a (line, column) pair, or an offset relative to the
enclosing item, or omit spans from the canonical form entirely if nothing
downstream reads them (canon is an EQUALITY comparand, not a diagnostic).
Whichever is chosen, state in dispatch-matrix.md`s comparand section what the
canonical form is stable under.

DISTINCT FROM fz-kdt.19, which is about the fixture matrix subtracting a
fixture`s leading-comment LINE COUNT from a gutter rendered out of a
`runtime:` source. This one is about byte offsets inside the canon dump and
needs no line-count change at all. Concordant: fz-f98.21 (the canonical form
itself), fz-kdt.211 (the other false-mover source -- an AOT executable
embedding the compiler`s build path).

RED-FIRST: the reproducer above yields zero canon diff lines.
title: Canon spans are byte offsets, so rewriting a fixture COMMENT is a canon mover by construction and a false signal in any base-vs-head comparand
